steps.intent: Our objective is a six-month, tightly conditioned renewal limited to Bab al-Hawa, with strong emphasis on cross-line deliveries, Syrian sovereignty and transparency, while avoiding language that would invite a veto by the United States, United Kingdom or France. We expect the main difficulties to be Western insistence on a longer twelve-month extension and additional crossings, and disagreement over references to the Syrian Government’s role and the impact of unilateral sanctions.

messages.Albania: Albania supports renewal of the Bab al-Hawa mechanism, but we cannot accept a six-month extension or conditionality that makes humanitarian access hostage to reporting. We ask for a twelve-month renewal and for language confirming that cross-border and cross-line deliveries are complementary and based solely on need, not subject to arbitrary interference. These changes are essential to ensure the Council responds to the humanitarian situation in Syria.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports renewing the Bab al-Hawa authorization and welcomes the focus on early recovery, but the text must not condition or subordinate cross-border aid to cross-line deliveries 'where feasible'. We ask for a longer, predictable renewal and for OP4 to affirm that cross-border and cross-line operations are complementary and needs-based. Brazil would also welcome explicit language that sanctions, including unilateral coercive measures, do not impede humanitarian action.
messages.China: The Chinese delegation supports the Russian draft as a basis, since it reflects the temporary and exceptional nature of the cross-border mechanism and the need to expand cross-line deliveries. We ask that OP6 explicitly refer to unilateral coercive measures and call for effective humanitarian exemptions, as unilateral sanctions are a main obstacle to improving the humanitarian situation. We also ask that OP3 and OP4 make clear that cross-line operations are conducted with full respect for Syria's sovereignty and in coordination with the Syrian authorities. With these improvements, China is ready to support the text.
messages.France: France supports renewing the Bab al-Hawa authorization before it expires and thanks the Russian Federation for circulating a draft. We cannot accept a six-month horizon or language that subordinates the cross-border mechanism to cross-line progress or to Syrian consent; the Council's authorization must remain predictable, needs-based and independent. We therefore ask for a twelve-month renewal, a balanced PP3, and neutral complementary language on cross-border and cross-line deliveries in OP4.
messages.Gabon: Gabon thanks the Russian Federation for the draft and supports renewing the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism. To meet the scale of need, Gabon asks for a twelve-month extension and for clear language that cross-line deliveries complement, rather than replace or condition, cross-border assistance. We also seek reporting language that preserves transparency without making humanitarian access contingent on cross-line progress.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa mechanism and welcomes the focus on early recovery, but the humanitarian situation requires predictable access and should not face another shutdown in six months. We therefore ask the penholder to provide a longer extension, or at least an additional six-month extension, and to make clear that cross-border and cross-line deliveries are complementary and needs-based rather than subordinating the cross-border mechanism. Transparency and full respect for humanitarian principles remain essential.
messages.India: India supports the extension of the Bab al-Hawa mechanism and welcomes the draft’s balanced emphasis on cross-line access, transparency and early recovery. To avoid repeated disruptions and provide predictability for the 3.4 million people in north-west Syria, India requests that OP2 include the additional six-month extension until 10 July 2023, subject to the Secretary-General’s substantive report, as provided in resolution 2585 (2021). With that change, India can support the draft.
messages.Ireland: Ireland supports renewing the Bab al-Hawa authorization and preventing a humanitarian cliff, but we cannot accept the current six-month duration. We ask for a twelve-month extension and for OP4 to be reframed so that cross-border deliveries are not subordinated to cross-line operations; the two must be complementary and needs-based. We also seek language that does not condition the authorization on the Secretary-General's report, while retaining robust reporting.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the Russian draft as a basis and is prepared to vote in favour, but we ask the penholder to strengthen the humanitarian logic of the text. We request a twelve-month renewal in OP2 and ask that OP4 clarify that cross-line deliveries complement, rather than replace or receive artificial priority over, cross-border operations, with all modalities driven by humanitarian need and principles.
messages.Mexico: We thank the Russian Federation for circulating this draft and can support a timely renewal of the Bab al-Hawa mechanism. Mexico urges a twelve-month extension to give humanitarian actors predictable planning and funding, and we ask that cross-border and cross-line deliveries be treated as complementary and needs-based, not one subordinated to the other. All humanitarian modalities must follow the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence and be driven solely by assessed needs.
messages.Norway: Norway supports renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism, but we cannot support the draft as written. We need a twelve-month extension until 10 July 2023, without making the mechanism subject to a report, and we need the text to make clear that cross-line deliveries complement rather than replace or condition cross-border assistance. We also ask you to delete the instruction in OP4 to prioritize cross-line deliveries where feasible.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE thanks the Russian Federation for its efforts to ensure the continuation of the Bab al-Hawa mechanism and supports the draft's humanitarian focus. We would prefer a twelve-month renewal to provide predictability for donors and humanitarian partners, and we ask that OP4 clarify that cross-border and cross-line deliveries are complementary and must not be subordinated to one another. We also suggest explicitly referring to the north-west and to assistance without discrimination. The UAE stands ready to work with all Council members to avoid any interruption of aid.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks the Russian Federation for circulating a draft, but we cannot support a six-month renewal that falls short of the UN’s assessed needs. We will push for a 12-month extension of the Bab al-Hawa crossing, together with Bab al-Salam, without conditionality. We cannot accept language that subordinates cross-border deliveries to cross-line progress; humanitarian access must be determined by need and international humanitarian law, with all modalities scaled up in parallel.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support the draft as currently drafted. We need a 12-month renewal of the cross-border mechanism and the inclusion of Bab al-Salam to meet humanitarian needs; a six-month, single-crossing mandate is inadequate. We also oppose language that prioritizes cross-line deliveries over cross-border operations and that implies the Syrian authorities have primary responsibility for humanitarian access; these should be corrected. We stand ready to work with the penholder to achieve a text that can command consensus.

steps.summary: The Russian revision retains the six-month, single-crossing Bab al-Hawa authorization subject to the Secretary-General's report, while incorporating limited complementarity, sovereignty, reporting and sanctions-exemption language. It rejects the core Western demands for a twelve-month renewal, Bab al-Salam and deconditioning, but is expected to secure enough support to pass with Western abstentions.

messages.Albania: Albania appreciates the partial acceptance of our earlier proposals, but the current text still falls short of what is needed to ensure predictable humanitarian access. A twelve-month renewal is essential, and the Bab al-Hawa authorization should not be made conditional on the Secretary-General's report or on cross-line progress; cross-border and cross-line deliveries must be complementary and needs-based. We also cannot accept language that singles out lawful sanctions as 'unilateral coercive measures' or implies over-compliance. We will support a text that reflects these points.
messages.Brazil: Brazil welcomes the reflected language on complementarity and humanitarian exemptions, but remains concerned that a six-month renewal and the reference to a phased transition away from cross-border delivery create damaging uncertainty for humanitarian operations in north-west Syria. We therefore ask the penholder to extend the authorization to twelve months, or at minimum provide an automatic additional six-month renewal, and to remove language that subordinates cross-border assistance to cross-line progress. Brazil can support the text once these humanitarian access concerns are addressed.
messages.China: China supports the revised Russian draft as a basis and welcomes the inclusion of sovereignty, coordination with the Syrian authorities, and a phased transition from cross-border to cross-line delivery. We have one remaining important request in OP6: an explicit call for the lifting of unilateral coercive measures, including unilateral sanctions, where they impede humanitarian access and early recovery activities. This reflects the concerns repeatedly raised by the Secretary-General and OHCHR and should not prevent Council unity. China is ready to join consensus on this basis.
messages.France: France welcomes the partial acceptance of complementarity and all-party access, but the current text still falls short. France cannot support language that subordinates the Council-authorized cross-border mechanism to the Syrian authorities, conditions its renewal, or introduces a phased transition away from it; nor can we accept the reference to 'unilateral coercive measures'. We need a twelve-month, needs-based renewal with the independence of humanitarian action clearly preserved.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the revised OP4's recognition that cross-border and cross-line deliveries are complementary, but we cannot accept language that could make cross-line a substitute for the cross-border mechanism while humanitarian needs remain so acute. We ask for this explicit clarification in OP4; with it, Gabon can support the six-month extension as a compromise and urges transparent, needs-based implementation.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the current text as a pragmatic compromise that keeps the Bab al-Hawa humanitarian lifeline open. We welcome the needs-based complementarity language in OP4 and the six-month renewal, and we urge the Council to adopt the draft without further delay. We call on all parties to ensure full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria.
messages.India: India supports the current text and will vote in favour. We appreciate the penholder’s partial acceptance of our earlier request and the inclusion of an intention to consider a further extension in light of the Secretary-General’s substantive report. Given the urgent humanitarian needs in Syria, we believe the Council should renew the Bab al-Hawa authorization without further delay and ensure predictable, needs-based humanitarian access, including through strengthened cross-line deliveries and early recovery support.
messages.Ireland: Ireland thanks the penholder for reflecting cross-line scaling in OP4, but we cannot support the current text without a twelve-month extension and without conditioning the authorization on a report. We also need OP4 to drop the 'phased transition' language and instead affirm that cross-border deliveries remain a lifeline as long as humanitarian needs require. These points remain essential for Ireland.
messages.Kenya: Kenya appreciates the partial acceptance on complementarity in OP4 and remains committed to a humanitarian mechanism driven by assessed needs. We still seek greater predictability through a six-plus-six-month extension and language that safeguards cross-border operations from being prematurely replaced by cross-line deliveries. Kenya can support the text with these changes.
messages.Mexico: Mexico welcomes the incorporation of non-discrimination in OP3 and needs-based complementarity in OP4. Our principal remaining concern is OP2: a six-month authorization is insufficient for predictable humanitarian planning and funding, and we therefore ask that it be extended to twelve months, until 10 July 2023, as was done in resolution 2585 (2021). Mexico can support the text with that change and remains committed to a humanitarian-focused renewal that preserves full, safe and unhindered access to all persons in need.
messages.Norway: Norway supports the current draft as a necessary compromise to prevent the expiry of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism and a devastating humanitarian gap. We regret that the extension is limited to six months and that deconditioning was not achieved, but we will vote in favour in the interest of continued humanitarian access. We call on all parties to ensure that cross-line deliveries complement and do not replace or condition cross-border assistance.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE thanks the penholder for reflecting our language on complementarity and access to the north-west. We can accept the six-month extension as a compromise, but we cannot accept language that makes cross-border assistance contingent on progress on cross-line deliveries. We therefore ask that OP4 be revised to make clear that cross-border and cross-line deliveries are complementary and needs-based, without subordinating the cross-border mechanism to cross-line progress.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom remains deeply concerned by the Russian draft's six-month, single-crossing mandate and its conditionality. Cross-border assistance is an essential humanitarian lifeline, and the Council should renew it for 12 months and preserve Bab al-Hawa and Bab al-Salam, without linking it to cross-line progress or Syrian regime coordination. We also need language that does not weaken sanctions or counter-terrorism safeguards. If these core concerns are not addressed, the UK will find it difficult to support the text.
messages.United States of America: The United States appreciates the penholder's efforts and the movement on complementarity and humanitarian exemptions. However, the current OP2 does not provide the predictability needed for humanitarian operations; we cannot accept a six-month-only renewal with a mere intention to consider an extension. We ask the penholder to include an additional six-month extension subject to the Secretary-General's report and, if possible, to restore the Bab al-Salam crossing.

steps.summary: The revised draft retains Russian priorities on sovereignty, conditionality, a single crossing, cross-line transition, and unilateral coercive measures, while adding a conditional additional six months and safeguards on cross-border availability. It is expected to secure 12 votes in favour, with France, the United Kingdom and the United States abstaining.

reasons.Albania: Albania votes in favour to preserve the cross-border humanitarian mechanism and prevent a lapse in aid, despite its red-line request for a 12-month unconditional extension not being met. It would likely reserve any explanation for after the vote rather than speak before it.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil supported the compromise because it extends humanitarian access with a longer mandate and includes safeguards against making cross-border aid contingent on cross-line progress, consistent with its negotiation requests and record of supporting humanitarian resolutions. Although the phased-transition language was retained, the added protection addressed Brazil’s core concern.
reasons.China: The draft accommodates China’s key request on unilateral coercive measures and preserves a temporary, sovereignty-respecting renewal of the cross-border mechanism. Voting in favour is consistent with China’s established position and its support for the Russian compromise text.
reasons.France: France abstains because the Russian draft falls short of its requested twelve-month deconditioned renewal and retains problematic language on Syrian authorities and transition, but vetoing would risk shutting a vital humanitarian lifeline. This matches France’s practice of allowing aid to continue while expressing strong reservations.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon abstained because its red-line request to replace the reference to a phased transition from cross-border to cross-line delivery was not fully accepted, while it did not want to block a humanitarian extension. The draft's partial safeguards were insufficient to overcome that concern.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana’s stated position in the last negotiation round was support, and its foreign policy prioritizes humanitarian access, Council unity and respect for Syrian sovereignty. A vote in favour is consistent with that record and with Ghana’s earlier support for renewing humanitarian mechanisms.
reasons.India: India's last-round position was support with no requested changes, consistent with its consistent backing for cross-border humanitarian renewals while upholding Syrian sovereignty. It will vote in favour and likely explain its vote after the vote rather than before.
reasons.Ireland: Ireland’s red-line request for a twelve-month, unconditional extension was rejected; the Russian draft retains a conditional six-plus-six arrangement and phased-transition language that Ireland cannot support given its humanitarian policy.
reasons.Kenya: Kenya’s last-round position was support with changes, and its key requests were at least partially accepted. It has consistently supported humanitarian renewals and practical access modalities, so a yes vote is consistent with its record.
reasons.Mexico: Mexico supported the draft in negotiations but its key request for a twelve-month renewal was rejected; the text also contains problematic language on transition and coordination that Mexico fears could weaken humanitarian principles. Therefore, consistent with its principled stance and actual vote on the Russian counter-draft, Mexico abstains.
reasons.Norway: Norway's last negotiation position was support with no requested changes, and the draft provides for a continued cross-border mechanism consistent with Norway's humanitarian priorities. Therefore Norway votes in favour.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the sponsor of the draft, Russia would vote in favour and use the pre-vote floor to justify its text, emphasizing sovereignty, cross-line access and opposition to unilateral sanctions.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: UAE supported renewing cross-border humanitarian aid but had unresolved concerns over the draft’s phased-transition language in OP4 and its treatment of unilateral coercive measures in OP6, so it abstained. It did not take the floor before the vote.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK’s red lines—12 months, Bab al-Salam access, deconditioning, and deletion of the unilateral coercive measures language—were rejected, so voting against aligns with its stated policy and prior positions.
reasons.United States of America: The United States would abstain: the draft extends the Bab al-Hawa mechanism but omits the needed Bab al-Salam crossing and contains problematic language on unilateral coercive measures. It would not speak before the vote, reserving its explanation for after the vote.

before.Brazil: Brazil votes in favour of this resolution. We welcome the extension of the cross-border mechanism at Bab al-Hawa and the provision for an additional six-month extension upon the Secretary-General’s substantive report, which we had called for in order to provide predictability for humanitarian operations. We also note that our proposal to ensure that cross-border assistance is not made contingent on progress in cross-line deliveries was partially reflected. While we retain concerns about the reference to a phased transition, the safeguard that cross-border assistance should not be prejudiced or subordinated to progress on cross-line access is essential. Brazil reaffirms that humanitarian assistance must be delivered in accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence and must reach all Syrians in need without discrimination. We stress that unilateral coercive measures should not impede humanitarian and early recovery activities. We urge all parties to facilitate safe, unhindered and sustained access, and we remain committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and to a political solution to the conflict.
before.China: China thanks the Russian Federation for presenting this draft. China has consistently maintained that humanitarian assistance to Syria must respect Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and be provided in accordance with the guiding principles of emergency humanitarian assistance. We support a pragmatic extension of the cross-border mechanism, which remains temporary and exceptional, and we believe that the draft appropriately emphasizes cross-line deliveries and a phased transition. We welcome the inclusion of language calling for the lifting of unilateral coercive measures where they impede humanitarian access and early recovery. China will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.France: France will abstain on this draft. We do so despite our grave concerns: the text does not provide the predictable twelve-month renewal that the humanitarian situation demands, and it retains language that risks subordinating humanitarian delivery to the consent of the Syrian authorities and that points toward a phased transition away from the cross-border mechanism. The references to unilateral coercive measures are also misplaced in this humanitarian resolution. France recalls that the cross-border mechanism was established by the Security Council and must not be dependent on the Syrian regime. Yet, given the catastrophic humanitarian needs and the imperative of preserving lifesaving access, France will not block the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa crossing. We urge the Council to return to a more robust and predictable humanitarian mandate.
before.Ghana: Ghana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains grave, and the continuation of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism is essential to sustain life-saving assistance to millions of people in need, especially in north-west Syria. We support the renewal while stressing that cross-border and cross-line deliveries must be complementary and must fully respect humanitarian principles, as well as Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We also underscore that sanctions and counter-terrorism measures must not impede humanitarian access and early recovery activities. Ghana calls on all parties to ensure full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all parts of Syria and to work in good faith towards a predictable and needs-based arrangement that reaches all Syrians without discrimination.
before.Ireland: Ireland recognises the grave humanitarian situation in Syria and remains committed to ensuring full, safe, unhindered and predictable humanitarian access to all civilians in need. We engaged constructively on this draft, but our core concerns have not been met. The cross-border mechanism is a lifeline for millions in north-west Syria, and it should be renewed on the basis of assessed humanitarian need, not made conditional on progress in cross-line operations or a phased transition that risks undermining the availability and predictability of assistance. For these reasons, Ireland will vote against this draft resolution. We remain ready to support a principled renewal that preserves and strengthens humanitarian access for the Syrian people.
before.Kenya: Kenya will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains grave, and the Council has a responsibility to ensure that the Bab al-Hawa crossing continues to provide life-saving assistance without interruption. We thank the penholder for engaging with our proposals, particularly the inclusion of the conditional additional six months in OP2 and the safeguard in OP4 that cross-border assistance should not be prejudiced or subordinated to progress on cross-line access. While Kenya continues to have some concerns about the phased-transition framing, we support cross-border and cross-line delivery based on assessed humanitarian needs and the United Nations guiding principles of humanitarian assistance. On that basis, we will vote in favour.
before.Mexico: Mexico thanks the Russian Federation for presenting this draft, but we will abstain. Mexico has consistently supported a twelve-month renewal of the cross-border mechanism to provide predictable, life-saving humanitarian assistance to millions of Syrians in need. While we recognize the draft’s six-month extension with a conditional additional six months, we regret that it does not provide the certainty requested by humanitarian actors and the Secretary-General. We are also concerned that references to a phased transition from cross-border to cross-line delivery, and to coordination with Syrian authorities, could be applied in ways that undermine the humanitarian principles of neutrality, impartiality and independence, as well as the primacy of assessed needs. Mexico supports expanding cross-line deliveries, but these must complement, not replace, cross-border assistance. We also affirm that unilateral coercive measures should not impede humanitarian access, but this draft as a whole does not meet the standard we believe is necessary. For these reasons, Mexico abstains.
before.Norway: Norway welcomes the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism through Bab al-Hawa, which remains a lifeline for millions of people in north-west Syria. We support this resolution as a necessary step to ensure that life-saving assistance continues to reach those in need. At the same time, we emphasize the need for full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all parts of Syria, and for cross-line deliveries to be strengthened in line with humanitarian principles. Norway will vote in favour.
before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. Our text is a balanced and practical response to the humanitarian needs of all Syrians. It preserves the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, focuses on expanding cross-line deliveries from within Syria, and insists that cross-border assistance remain temporary and exceptional. We are also convinced that unilateral coercive measures must not impede humanitarian access and early recovery. We call on all Council members to support this resolution, which is aimed at alleviating the suffering of the Syrian people and ensuring the transparent and effective delivery of assistance.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr President, the United Kingdom has engaged constructively on this draft, and we recognize that some safeguards have been added. But the text still does not meet the humanitarian requirements the Council has repeatedly identified. Cross-border assistance remains a lifeline for millions of Syrians, and the United Kingdom cannot support a draft that limits access to one crossing, attaches unacceptable conditions to renewal, or risks subordinating cross-border relief to cross-line progress in a way that is not driven by humanitarian need. We also oppose the language on unilateral coercive measures: sanctions contain humanitarian exemptions and safeguards, and this draft’s approach is inappropriate and divisive. For these reasons, the United Kingdom will vote against this draft. We continue to call for a 12-month renewal covering Bab al-Hawa and Bab al-Salam, determined by need and consistent with humanitarian principles.

after.Albania:
Mr President,

Albania voted in favour of this draft resolution because the continuation of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border operation is a humanitarian imperative. We regret that the Council was unable to adopt it.

The text before us was not the text we would have written. We shared the concerns expressed about the lack of a predictable twelve-month renewal, about conditionality, and about language that could risk subordinating cross-border assistance to political or bureaucratic considerations. We also did not believe that the reference to unilateral coercive measures belonged in this humanitarian resolution. But in the face of catastrophic humanitarian needs, we chose to support the only text on the table that would have kept life-saving cross-border assistance flowing to millions of Syrians in need.

The failure to renew this mechanism is not a victory for anyone. It is a blow to the most vulnerable. The Security Council must not leave a gap in humanitarian access. We call on all members to act responsibly and without delay to ensure full, safe, unhindered and predictable humanitarian access to all parts of Syria, including the north-west, on the basis of assessed humanitarian need and in accordance with the United Nations guiding principles of humanitarian assistance. Cross-border assistance must not be replaced or made conditional. Cross-line deliveries must be strengthened and must be complementary, not a precondition.

Albania remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria. We urge all parties to respect international humanitarian law and to protect civilians. We stand ready to engage constructively on a principled renewal that meets the scale of the humanitarian emergency.

Thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,
China voted in favour of the draft resolution and regrets that the Council has not been able to adopt it. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains grave, and the uninterrupted delivery of humanitarian assistance is of the utmost importance. China has consistently held that humanitarian assistance must respect Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and must be provided in accordance with the guiding principles of humanitarian emergency assistance. The cross-border mechanism is temporary and exceptional and should be gradually improved in light of the situation on the ground, with efforts to strengthen cross-line deliveries. We also reiterate that unilateral coercive measures are a major obstacle to improving the humanitarian situation and should not impede humanitarian access or early recovery. China calls on all Council members to put the Syrian people first, avoid politicization, maintain unity and continue consultations with a view to reaching a balanced and practical arrangement that ensures the effective and transparent delivery of humanitarian assistance.
after.Gabon:
Mr President,

Gabon abstained in the vote on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. We did so after careful reflection. The humanitarian situation in Syria is grave, and the Bab al-Hawa crossing remains a lifeline for millions of civilians in north-west Syria. Gabon supports a predictable renewal of the cross-border mechanism on the basis of assessed humanitarian needs and in full respect of the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence.

We were not in a position to support this text because it does not provide the twelve-month predictability that humanitarian actors have repeatedly called for and because its provisions on conditionality and a phased transition carry risks for the availability and predictability of cross-border assistance. At the same time, Gabon did not vote against the draft, as we do not wish to block life-saving relief. We recall the importance of full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all parts of Syria, including through both cross-border and cross-line deliveries, while respecting Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.

Gabon regrets that the Council could not reach a consensus and urges all members to work constructively towards a principled and predictable renewal that places the needs of the Syrian people above political differences. We remain ready to engage.
after.Ghana: Thank you, Mr. President. Ghana takes the floor to express our deep regret that the Council has not been able to adopt the draft resolution before us. With the current authorization for the Bab al-Hawa crossing due to expire in two days, the failure to act today places millions of civilians in north-west Syria at grave risk. Ghana voted in favour because we believe that the cross-border mechanism remains a lifeline that must be preserved on the basis of assessed humanitarian need and in full accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. At the same time, we reiterate that cross-border and cross-line deliveries must be complementary, not mutually exclusive, and must respect Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. The Council cannot afford to remain divided while humanitarian needs continue to rise. We urge all members to return immediately to constructive negotiations in a spirit of compromise and Council unity, so that a predictable and principled renewal can be secured without further delay. Ghana stands ready to work with all members to prevent a humanitarian catastrophe and to uphold the Council’s responsibility to the Syrian people.
after.India:
Mr. President,

India voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. We thank the Russian Federation for its efforts to present a text that would have ensured the continued delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance through the Bab al-Hawa crossing, while also emphasizing the importance of cross-line deliveries and respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.

We regret that the draft was not adopted. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains grave, with millions of civilians in need of assistance. At this critical juncture, the Council should not leave a gap in the provision of humanitarian relief. India has consistently called for enhanced and effective humanitarian assistance to all Syrians throughout the country, without discrimination, politicization or preconditions, and in accordance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence.

India supports the renewal of the cross-border mechanism at Bab al-Hawa and believes that cross-border and cross-line deliveries should be complementary and based on assessed humanitarian needs. We also underline that humanitarian assistance must not be made hostage to political considerations. We urge all parties to facilitate full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all parts of Syria and call upon the Council to work constructively and urgently to ensure predictability in humanitarian operations and to avoid any interruption in assistance to the Syrian people.
after.Kenya:
Mr. President,

Kenya regrets that the Council was unable to adopt this draft resolution, especially with the current cross-border authorization due to expire in a matter of days. We voted in favour because the Bab al-Hawa crossing remains a lifeline for millions of Syrians in north-west Syria who depend on humanitarian assistance for their survival. While Kenya had concerns about the phased-transition framing, we supported this text in the interest of preventing an interruption in life-saving aid.

The failure to reach agreement today should not become a failure to the Syrian people. We therefore urge all Council members to return to negotiations in a spirit of compromise and to act with urgency before the deadline. The renewal of the cross-border mechanism must be based on assessed humanitarian needs and the United Nations guiding principles of humanitarian assistance, while we continue to support efforts to strengthen cross-line deliveries in full respect of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity.

Kenya will remain engaged and calls on the Council to show the unity and resolve that the humanitarian situation in Syria demands.
after.Norway:
Mr. President,

Norway regrets that the Council has been unable to adopt this resolution. The renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism is a humanitarian necessity, and the timing is critical: millions of people in north-west Syria depend on this lifeline. Norway voted in favour because maintaining that operation is essential and because a failure to act would have immediate and grave consequences for civilians.

At the same time, Norway has consistently stressed that cross-border and cross-line deliveries must be complementary and must be based on assessed humanitarian needs and the United Nations guiding principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. Cross-border assistance must not be subordinated to political progress or to the consent of the Syrian authorities. We regret that the text did not fully meet these concerns, but we considered it important to avoid an interruption of life-saving assistance.

The Council cannot allow the humanitarian response to become a casualty of political division. Norway urges all members to return to constructive negotiations without delay and to ensure the predictable, safe and unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to all parts of Syria. We remain ready to work with all delegations to that end.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation regrets that the draft resolution submitted by our delegation was not adopted. It was a balanced, pragmatic and realistic text. It would have preserved the humanitarian delivery mechanism through Bab al-Hawa for six months, with the possibility of a further six months, while confirming the temporary and exceptional nature of the cross-border mechanism and strengthening cross-line deliveries from within Syria in full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. It also addressed the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures on humanitarian access and early recovery.

The result of the vote is telling. Eight Council members supported the draft, but the required number of votes was not reached. We regret that some delegations preferred abstention or opposition to a solution that could have helped millions of Syrians. Once again, the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people have been made hostage to political calculations and to the anti-Syrian agenda of certain Western members. Those who voted against or abstained bear their share of responsibility for the Council’s failure to send a clear and unified humanitarian signal.

We thank those delegations that supported our text. The Russian Federation will continue to insist that humanitarian assistance to Syria be provided in accordance with international humanitarian law and the guiding principles of the United Nations, without politicization, discrimination or illegal unilateral sanctions. We will not support attempts to impose indefinite or open-ended cross-border mechanisms that violate Syria’s sovereignty and bypass the Syrian authorities. We remain ready for constructive work on a realistic and respectful basis.

Thank you.
after.United Arab Emirates:
Mr. President,

The United Arab Emirates abstained on the draft resolution before the Council. We did so because the humanitarian situation in Syria remains dire, and the Bab al-Hawa crossing continues to be a lifeline for millions of civilians in north-west Syria. We have consistently supported a predictable renewal of the cross-border mechanism so that humanitarian actors can plan and deliver assistance without interruption.

At the same time, we recognize the importance of expanding cross-line deliveries and early recovery projects, and of respecting Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. However, we are concerned that some provisions could introduce conditionality or uncertainty into cross-border assistance. Humanitarian access must be based on assessed needs and the guiding principles of humanitarian assistance, and cross-border and cross-line deliveries should be complementary rather than one being subordinate to the other.

We also stress that sanctions and counter-terrorism measures must not impede humanitarian assistance and early recovery. The Council must not allow political differences to interrupt lifesaving aid. We urge all members to engage constructively to ensure the continuation of the cross-border mechanism and to reach a balanced and predictable extension that meets the needs of the Syrian people.

Thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr President, the United Kingdom regrets that the Council has not been able to adopt a resolution renewing the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism. We voted against this draft because it did not provide the predictable twelve-month renewal that the Secretary-General and humanitarian actors have said is essential, and because it risked subordinating cross-border assistance to progress on cross-line operations and to the consent of the Syrian authorities. The cross-border mechanism is a lifeline for millions of Syrians. It must be renewed on the basis of assessed humanitarian need and in full respect for humanitarian principles. We also remain firmly opposed to the inappropriate language on unilateral coercive measures. The United Kingdom remains ready to work with all Council members on a principled renewal that preserves full, safe, unhindered and predictable humanitarian access. We urge the Council to act without delay.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States abstained on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. We did so because, while we strongly support the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism, this text fell short of what the humanitarian situation requires and what this Council has repeatedly committed to. It failed to provide the predictable twelve-month renewal that United Nations humanitarian actors have said is essential. It introduced conditionalities and a phased transition that could subordinate cross-border assistance to the consent of the Syrian authorities and to progress on cross-line deliveries, rather than to assessed humanitarian need. And it included divisive language on unilateral coercive measures that is inappropriate in a humanitarian resolution and misrepresents the fact that United States sanctions contain robust humanitarian exemptions and do not target humanitarian assistance.

The United States has consistently supported a clean, predictable twelve-month renewal of the cross-border mechanism, as we did in resolution 2585 (2021). We regret that the Council has not been able to unite around such a renewal today. We abstained rather than voting against this text because we recognized the urgent need to preserve cross-border access, but we could not vote in favour of a resolution that risks undermining the very mechanism it purports to renew. We remain deeply concerned that the failure to adopt a predictable renewal will only increase uncertainty for millions of Syrians in need.

We call on all Council members to return to negotiations in good faith and to put the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people above political considerations. The United States will continue to work with partners to ensure that life-saving assistance reaches all Syrians in need, in accordance with humanitarian principles. Thank you.
